newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 6.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Armed forces commander General Feisal Tanjung said Malaysia has the right to close the checkpoints on the border with Indonesia's west Kalimantan following riots in the province. Indonesia shares the huge Borneo island with Malaysia and Brunei.

Indonesia's consumer price index rose 1.03 percent in January and its trade surplus last November dropped to $764.6 million. The January inflation rate of 1.03 percent was higher than the 0.55 percent figure recorded in December, but lower than the 2.16 percent in January, 1996.

European, American and South Korean businessmen have expressed great concern about the new customs clearance rules the Indonesian government plans to implement in April. The government plans to introduce selective non-arrival inspections of imports and post-entry auditing of documents.

Former OPEC secretary-general Subroto has criticised the government for its handling of the huge Busang gold mine in Indonesia's east Kalimantan province. Subroto, who is a former Indonesian energy minister, said the government should not have set a deadline for Canadian Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp to settle their dispute over share equity.
Ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, is expected to face police questioning on Thursday for allegedly organising an illegal meeting at her residence.
